reason: This text passage (Genesis 32-33) focuses on Jacob's personal journey, his encounter with the divine at Peniel, and his reconciliation with Esau. The prayer section explicitly affirms God's faithfulness and covenant loyalty to Jacob ('all the loving-kindness and all the truth that you have done to your servant'). The passage contains no statement or suggestion that God lacks loyalty to the people or considers replacing them with another nation. The theological claim in the statement—that Yahweh might abandon Israel for a different people—is entirely absent from this narrative.
